purpose: Realize the first Branch FLINTLOCK-equivalent fast-carrier suppression cycle against an alerted/dispersed Marshall air network, carrying forward Raiden/C2 and post-GALVANIC exchange maturation without granting either side magic detection or kill bonuses.
historical_baseline: Historical FLINTLOCK achieved launch-point surprise in squally/overcast weather and rapidly neutralized Roi/Taroa/Wotje/Kwajalein air power. Branch shifts the date and removes complete surprise while retaining US numerical/CIC/AA superiority.

target_split.priority: fighter sweep, runway, radar/radio/plot, dispersed aircraft
fighter sweep, runway, radar/communications, land-attack parking/dispersal
runways, radio/radar, shipping/AA opportunity targets; Eniwetok remains a later/secondary cycle target

US_first_cycle.reservation_guard: The 610 ready-aircraft TF58 center is not a 610-plane simultaneous strike. Large CAP/ASW/search/recovery reserves remain because Japanese fleet carriers are still unlocated.

Japanese_warning_and_launch.usable_warning: roughly 18-26 minutes at the best Taroa/Roi nodes before first major arrivals; shorter at damaged/outer nodes
Japanese_warning_and_launch.effect: Dispersal and staged readiness prevent a historical-style mass parking loss. A-grade/B+ warning creates favorable initial altitude/beam geometry for part of the defense, but US F6F/CIC escort mass still dominates prolonged combat.

centered_losses_through_09_00.loss_guard: These are first-cycle Branch working losses only. They do not rewrite GALVANIC or become a universal fixed-base exchange ratio.

base_effects.state_09_00: Radar/plot chain degraded but not erased; runway heavily cratered with emergency-use strip/sections recoverable on an hours-scale; dispersed aircraft and alternate revetments preserve a meaningful remnant.
base_effects.C2_grade_after: B/B+ until radar/plot repair restores A-/A function.

base_effects.state_09_00: Primary radar/communications node badly suppressed and runway intermittently usable; visual/DF/radio fragments still pass warning but fighter direction quality falls.
base_effects.C2_grade_after: B centered, locally lower during outages.

base_effects.state_09_00: Moderate runway/radio damage; still useful as a dispersed/staging node but not a full-strength independent fighter base.

post_cycle_marshall_air_state.accounting_note: Physical hull/airframe presence falls less than serviceability because several damaged aircraft remain repairable. Night-strike losses are included where applicable; do not subtract them twice.

reverse_bearing_contact.event: A surviving fast Japanese reconnaissance aircraft follows the reverse bearing of the first US strike stream and obtains a short visual on one US TG during recovery/reorganization.
reverse_bearing_contact.report: Three carrier decks strongly identified with three fast battleships/heavy screen; position roughly 120-160 nmi from the Kwajalein battle area; recovery/launch activity visible. Report transmitted before scout loss/forced disengagement.
reverse_bearing_contact.confidence: HIGH fresh contact on one US TG; other two TG positions remain insufficiently fresh.
reverse_bearing_contact.carrier_gate_result: Japanese first-line carrier GO remains WITHHELD. The holding force is still several hundred nautical miles west; a same-morning strike would be a long-margin launch, and the locations/mission state of the other US groups are not known well enough. The fresh report instead drives submarine convergence and conditional eastward carrier closure.

US_operational_assessment: First cycle succeeds in suppressing and degrading the Marshall air network but does not annihilate it. US commanders recognize materially stronger warning/dispersal and higher first-cycle losses than historical FLINTLOCK, reinforcing continued radar/communications/runway suppression before amphibious commitment.
Japan_operational_assessment: The warning system pays off by preventing decapitation and inflicting meaningful cost, but the numerical/system disparity remains decisive. Preserve scouts, submarines and remaining night-strike crews for mission-split opportunities rather than committing the three fleet carriers merely to defend fixed islands.
next_exact_action: Run 2 Feb late-morning/afternoon second suppression cycle and submarine convergence on the freshly reported TG. Resolve whether a CVL/AO/escort opportunity emerges and whether repeated US strikes collapse Taroa/Roi C2 before night.
